title: Prohibition on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels (BMC Chapter 13.63)
requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide a coordinated pricing algorithm to Berkeley landlords, and unlawful for a landlord to use one, to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley; each unit and each month of use is a separate violation. The City Attorney may sue over either the sale or the use, and an aggrieved tenant may sue a landlord over its use, for injunctive relief, damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
key_value: Ban on selling or using coordinated pricing algorithms; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; Competitor Data = non-public data less than 90 days old
coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Applies to landlords and to anyone who sells or licenses such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
exemptions: The following are excluded from the definition of coordinated pricing algorithm: (a) products or processes that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, occupancy rates or terms; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under local, state or federal affordable housing guidelines; (c) products or processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord.
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
penalty: City Attorney civil action for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees and costs if the City prevails. Aggrieved tenant civil action for injunctive relief, money damages and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees and costs if the tenant prevails.

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance: Annual General Adjustment limit on rent increases (as amended by Measure BB)
requirement: Landlords of fully covered units may raise rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), which the Rent Board sets at 65% of the Bay Area CPI increase and which Measure BB caps at 5%. Banked (unused) AGAs may still raise rent above 5% up to the rent ceiling, and Regulation 1148 sets the eligibility and tenant-notice conditions for taking the increase.

coverage_conditions: Fully covered (rent ceiling and AGA limit apply): most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually under separate leases). Government-subsidized units (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME) fall within these categories where Federal or State law does not prohibit rent control. Utility charges for fully covered units must be included in base rent unless the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to hold the account.
exemptions: Not subject to rent control (partially covered, registration only): new construction with a Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums. Exempt: 'Golden Duplex' units (owner-occupied on Dec. 31, 1979, with an owner currently living in one unit); units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the owner, if the owner lived on the property at the start of the tenancy. Section 202, Section 811, and HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgage projects with Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside or Project-based Section 8 subsidies are not rent-controlled. The 2026 AGA does not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

title: California Tenant Protection Act: just cause required to terminate tenancies
requirement: Once a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may terminate the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written termination notice. For no-fault terminations, the owner must either pay relocation assistance equal to one month's rent within 15 calendar days of serving the notice or waive the final month's rent.

coverage_conditions: Residential real property whose tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied it for the required period. The section does not apply to property covered by a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended later if that ordinance is more protective. exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, and adult residential facilities; school or university dormitories; tenants who share a bathroom or kitchen with an owner-occupant; owner-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes where the owner lived in one unit at the start of the tenancy; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property such as single-family homes or condominiums owned by natural persons, subject to the statute's conditions.
interaction: Does not apply to property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended after that date that is more protective than this section (the local ordinance applies instead). Yields to local rules: BERK-EVICT-01, BERK-EVICT-02, LA-EVICT-01, LA-EVICT-02, LA-EVICT-03, SD-EVICT-01, SF-EVICT-01, SA-EVICT-01.

penalty: A notice is void if the owner does not strictly comply. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, attorney's fees and costs at the court's discretion, and up to three times actual damages (plus punitive damages) for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct. title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act of 2019, AB 1482, as amended by SB 567)
requirement: Over any 12-month period, an owner of covered residential real property may not raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. The increase is measured against the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months, and no more than two increases are allowed in 12 months for the same tenant. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession.
key_value: 5% + local CPI-U change (April-to-April, rounded to the nearest 0.1%), capped at 10%; at most two increases per 12 months
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property, meaning any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park, unless exempt. Applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (mobilehome tenancies: on or after February 18, 2021). Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome. Units issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years are excluded on a rolling basis.
exemptions: (1) Deed-restricted or government-agreement affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households, or housing subject to an affordability subsidy agreement. (2) Dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school. (3) Housing subject to a local rent or price control ordinance that limits annual increases to less than the state cap. (4) Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless it is a mobilehome. (5) Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, such as single-family homes and condominiums. This exemption applies only if the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member, and the tenant was given the required written exemption notice (§ 1947.12(d)(5)). (6) A two-unit property in which the owner occupied the other unit for the entire tenancy.
interaction: Does not apply to housing subject to a local rent or price control ordinance that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap. The section does not expand or limit local governments' authority to adopt rent controls consistent with Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.). Yields to local rules: BERK-RENT-01, LA-RENT-01, SF-RENT-01, SA-RENT-01.

title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
requirement: Landlords of JCO units may end a tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause listed in the ordinance. Before a no-fault eviction they must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of serving notice. All eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service. Non-payment evictions are barred unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.

A natural-person single-family owner pays one month's rent. Non-payment eviction only if the amount owed exceeds Fair Market Rent, and eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days.
coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and a property with only one single-family dwelling. exemptions: Transient hotels; licensed care facilities; fraternity or sorority houses; the owner's roommate; cooperatives in certain circumstances; some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers; some HACLA- or government-owned properties; units already subject to the RSO; tenancies under 6 months where the original lease has not expired. No relocation is owed when one resident manager replaces another, or for natural-disaster hazards not caused by landlord negligence. Accumulated rent may be offset against relocation, except for government orders to vacate.

Las violaciones son ilegales bajo la Ley Antimonopolio estatal. Vigente el 1 de julio de 2027.

title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law: deposit cap, interest-bearing account, notice and 30-day return
requirement: If a landlord collects a security deposit, it may not exceed 1.5 times one month's rent, with any yearly increase capped at 10% of the current deposit. The deposit must be held in trust in an insured New Jersey interest-bearing account (interest belongs to the tenant), with written notice of the account details given to the tenant, and must be returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
key_value: Max deposit 1.5x one month's rent; yearly increase max 10% of current deposit; max 2.5x monthly rent at lease inception (deposit plus first month's rent); return within 30 days of tenancy termination (5 business days if tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation; 15 business days after a Safe Housing Act termination); double damages for wrongful withholding
coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may make the law apply 30 days after sending the landlord a written request.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant sends a written request, which takes effect after 30 days. The interest-bearing account provisions do not apply to seasonal rentals, meaning a term of 125 consecutive days or less by a person with a permanent residence elsewhere. The landlord bears the burden of proving seasonal use.
quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
subject: landlord
supporting_spans: The security deposit money continues to be the property of the person making the deposit
It does not matter how the prepaid funds are labeled.

plain_language.en: New Jersey caps a security deposit at 1.5 times one month's rent, with yearly increases limited to 10% of the current deposit. It must be held in an insured New Jersey interest-bearing account and returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days.

title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (good cause eviction)
requirement: A residential landlord may evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease only for a statutory good cause, through a court order, and after any required written Notice to Quit or Notice to Cease. Expiry of the lease term is not by itself a ground for eviction, and self-help evictions and lockouts are illegal.
key_value: Good cause required to evict or refuse renewal; Notice to Quit periods range from 3 days to 3 years depending on cause; relocation assistance of 6x monthly rent for illegal-occupancy evictions
coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes. Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are subject to a separate, shorter list of causes.
exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units (two- or three-unit owner-occupied buildings). Hotel or motel guests, and guest houses rented to transient or seasonal guests; hotel and motel occupants who reside there continually with no alternate residence are covered. A unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it.
quoted_span:
A landlord must have 
good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause 
eviction.
penalty: Self-help eviction or unlawful entry makes the landlord liable for damages, including court costs and reasonable attorney fees, and possible disorderly conduct charges.
subject: landlord
supporting_spans:
This law may not apply to two - or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or 
fewer rental units.

Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in 
an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

unless they have good cause not to renew the lease. The 
good causes for eviction are detailed under the section entitled, “Eviction,” (N.J.S.A. 2A:18:61.3).
Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey.

plain_language.en: New Jersey's Anti-Eviction Act allows a landlord to evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease only for a statutory good cause, through a court order, after any required written notice. Lease expiry alone is not a ground, and lockouts are illegal.
plain_language.es: La Ley Contra el Desalojo de Nueva Jersey permite desalojar o negarse a renovar un contrato solo por una causa justa establecida por ley, mediante orden judicial y tras el aviso escrito requerido. El vencimiento del contrato no basta, y los cierres de acceso son ilegales.
plain_language.renter: Your landlord can evict you or refuse to renew your lease only for a statutory good cause and through a court order; lockouts are illegal.
plain_language.landlord: You may evict or refuse to renew only for a statutory good cause, with any required written notice and a court order; lockouts are illegal.
plain_language.renter_es: Su propietario solo puede desalojarlo o negarse a renovar su contrato por una causa justa establecida por ley y mediante orden judicial; los cierres de acceso son ilegales.
plain_language.landlord_es: Usted solo puede desalojar o negarse a renovar por una causa justa establecida por ley, con el aviso escrito requerido y una orden judicial; los cierres de acceso son ilegales.

title: NJ cap on residential rental application fees ($50, CPI-adjusted)
requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee over $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental unit. Beginning January 1, 2027, the cap is adjusted annually for CPI increases only (the Division of Consumer Affairs publishes the limit). Violations carry penalties up to $500/$750/$1,000, and the overcharge is refunded to the applicant.

coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties for dwelling purposes (leases and subleases) statewide, other than the exempt categories below.

requirement.from: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes that exceeds $50. Beginning January 1 of the year next following enactment and each year after, the cap is adjusted in proportion to the percent change in the CPI (NY-Northern NJ-Long Island, All Urban Consumers, All Items) over the 12 months ending October 31 of the prior year. The adjustment is made only if the change is greater than zero. The Director of the Division of Consumer Affairs publishes the applicable limit annually on the division's website and adopts implementing rules, including a mechanism for applicants to report violations. The amount wrongfully charged is taken from the collected penalty and remitted to the applicant or prospective tenant.

title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law: 30-year exemption from local rent control

coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, for 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

interaction: Exempts newly constructed multiple dwellings from any local rent control ordinance for 30 years after completion.

Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period

plain_language.es: Nueva Jersey no tiene un límite estatal de alquiler, pero los municipios pueden adoptar control de alquileres. Los edificios multifamiliares recién construidos están exentos del control local de alquileres durante 30 años después de terminada la construcción.

title: New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal record screening limits)
requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer, except for methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration. After a conditional offer, they may consider only specified convictions within look-back periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment with written notice, an opportunity to appeal, and prior written disclosure of their criminal-history criteria.

exemptions: Excludes a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirements
requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of the just causes listed in Section 37.9(a), and that cause must be the dominant motive; expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause. Evictions for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of a unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation also require relocation payments under Section 37.9C.
key_value: 17 just cause reasons under Section 37.9(a)
coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. Some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits remain subject to the just cause eviction provisions. These include units whose first Certificate of Occupancy was issued after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
exemptions: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 rather than Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
penalty: Substantial civil and/or criminal liability for unlawful eviction or attempted eviction.
subject: landlord
supporting_spans: Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

plain_language.es: San Francisco permite que el propietario de una unidad cubierta desaloje solo por una de las causas justificadas de la Sección 37.9(a), y debe ser el motivo dominante. Algunos desalojos sin culpa también requieren pagos de reubicación según la Sección 37.9C.

title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance: annual allowable rent increase limits
requirement: For units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits, the annual allowable increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent (base rent × .016). The prior periods were 1.4% (3/1/2025–2/28/2026) and 1.7% (3/1/2024–2/28/2025).
key_value: 1.6% annual allowable increase for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 (previously 1.4% for 3/1/2025–2/28/2026)
coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, other than tenancies exempt from its rent increase limitations.
exemptions: Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency. These tenancies remain subject to the Ordinance's just cause eviction provisions.
